commands.name: handoff

commands.name: harness
commands.description: Operate the Harness agent fleet for this project — `/harness <idea>` takes an idea to a running fleet in one conversation (install, init, grill into a PRD, start); first-time SETUP (init, seed labels, start) and day-to-day operate (pause/resume/update/status, watch sessions, unstick the GitHub-issue board). commands.name: harness-arc

(user)

commands.name: harness-issue

commands.name: harness-one

commands.name: harness-pause

commands.name: harness-resume

commands.name: harness-start

commands.name: harness-status

commands.name: harness-stop

commands.name: harness-uninstall

commands.name: subagent-task-tree
commands.description: Execute a multi-task implementation plan as a chained subagent tree — you are the parent controller; you spawn one manager per task; each manager spawns a planner, a plan-auditor, one implementer per subtask, per-subtask auditors, and a final drift-auditor. (user)

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's recipe covers them) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify

commands.name: batch

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts

Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: google-workspace

Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. commands.name: computer-use
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: chrome-browser

It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's recipe covers them) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

## Problem Statement

A one-person online shop keeps its catalogue, stock movements and customer orders in three plain-text files. There is no tool that reads them reliably: nobody can see at a glance what is on the shelves and what needs buying, what an order costs (to the penny, with volume and order discounts and per-product tax), or what can ship today, and a typo in a file goes unnoticed.

## Solution

A pure-standard-library Python (>= 3.9) package **`stockroom`**, installable with `pip install .`, that is both an importable library (`import stockroom`) and a `stockroom` console command. It has two halves, built in this order because the second depends on the first:

1. **Shelves** — parse `catalog.txt` and `movements.txt`, stock levels, low-stock/buy list, per-product history, and appending stock-in / stock-out movements (`stock`, `low`, `history`, `receive`, `ship`).
2. **Orders** — parse `orders.txt`, exact penny pricing (`price_order`), `quote`, `fulfil` (ship what the shelves cover), `invoice` (price what has shipped) and `report` (text/csv/json).

The `## Original request` section at the bottom is the authoritative spec; this PRD only pins down the decisions it leaves open.

## User Stories

1. As the shop owner, I run `stockroom stock` and see every product's on-hand count and whether it is ok / low / out.
2. As the shop owner, I run `stockroom low` and get how many of each low or out product to buy.
3. As the shop owner, I run `stockroom history AB-100` and see every movement of that product with the running balance.
4. As the shop owner, I run `stockroom receive` / `stockroom ship` to record a delivery or a manual stock-out without hand-editing the file, and the tool refuses anything that would break the file's rules.
5. As the shop owner, I run `stockroom quote SO-1001` and get the exact priced order (volume discount, order discount, tax, total).
6. As the shop owner, I run `stockroom fulfil SO-1001 2024-03-10` and the tool ships what stock allows, records it, and tells me what is backordered.
7. As the shop owner, I run `stockroom invoice SO-1001` to bill what has actually shipped.
8. As the shop owner, I run `stockroom report` (text, csv or json) to see every order's status, units and money.
9. As the shop owner, when one of my files has a mistake the tool names the file and the line, and exits 1 without printing anything on standard output.
10. As a script author, I `import stockroom` and use `parse_catalog`, `parse_movements`, `parse_orders`, `stock_levels`, `price_order` and `ParseError`.
11. As the shop owner, `--json` output lets me feed results into other tools; piping into `head` never shows a traceback.

## Implementation Decisions

**Layout & packaging**
- `pyproject.toml` (setuptools backend, `requires-python = ">=3.9"`, no runtime dependencies), console script `stockroom = stockroom.cli:main`. Package `stockroom/` with at least `__init__.py` (re-exports the public API), `__main__.py` (`python -m stockroom`), a parsing module, a shelves/stock module, a pricing/orders module and `cli.py`. Python 3.9 compatible: no `match`, no runtime `X | Y` unions, no `dataclass(slots=...)`.
- Domain objects are dataclasses: `Product(sku, name, price: Decimal, reorder: int, tax: str)`, `Movement(date, sku, quantity, note, line)`, `Order(id, date, customer, lines: list[tuple[str,int]], line)`, `Quote(lines, subtotal, order_discount, tax, total)`, `QuoteLine(sku, quantity, unit, gross, discount, net)`. Extra fields (e.g. source line number) are fine.
- The CLI does not use `argparse` (it abbreviates long options and mangles dash-led values); it is a small hand-written parser.

**Reading files**
- Read bytes, decode strict UTF-8 (failure -> exit 2), drop one leading U+FEFF. Split on `\n` only, then remove one trailing `\r` per line (so CRLF works; a lone `\r` elsewhere is ordinary content). Do NOT use `str.splitlines()`.
- "Whitespace" for trimming, blank-line detection, comment detection and separators means space and tab only. A line is blank if it is empty after trimming; it is a comment if it starts with `#` after leading space/tab.
- Numbers are ASCII digits only (regexes, never bare `int()`, which accepts `1_000` and non-ASCII digits).
  - price: `^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]{1,2})?$` and >= 0.01 (`12.` and `.5` are mistakes; leading zeros allowed).
  - reorder: `^[0-9]+$` (no sign).
  - movement quantity: `^[+-]?[0-9]+$`, non-zero (`0`, `+0`, `-00` are mistakes).
  - order line quantity: `^[0-9]+$`, >= 1.
- SKU: `^[A-Za-z]{2,4}-[0-9]{3}$`, stored upper case. Order id: `^[Ss][Oo]-[0-9]+$`, stored upper case (digits kept as typed). Date: `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$` and a real calendar date.
- Catalogue: 4 or 5 `|`-separated fields; tax case-insensitive, stored lower case; duplicate SKU is reported on the second line.
- Movements: at least 3 whitespace-separated fields; note = rest of the line after the quantity field, trimmed. Lines are first all parsed in file order (first syntax error wins); then the stock check runs over the movements stable-sorted by date and reports the first movement (in that order) that takes a product below zero, by its own file line number.
- Orders: exactly 4 fields; LINES split on `,` (empty piece is a mistake); duplicate SKU within an order and duplicate order id are mistakes.
- `ParseError(ValueError)` has `.line`; `str(err)` starts with `line N: ` followed by a short description. The CLI prints `stockroom: <file>: line N: ...` on stderr.
- Commands read only their files, in the order catalogue, movements, orders; the first file mistake wins.

**Stock**
- Movements count stably sorted by date. `stock_levels` covers every catalogue SKU. Status: `out` = 0, `low` = 0 < onhand <= reorder, `ok` otherwise. `low` BUY = `max(1, 2*reorder - onhand)`. Sorting "by SKU" = plain string order of the upper-case SKU.

**Pricing** (`Decimal`, `ROUND_HALF_UP` to `0.01` at every rounding step)
- Per line: gross = qty x unit; volume discount 10 % if qty >= 50, else 5 % if qty >= 10, else 0; net = gross - discount.
- subtotal = sum of nets; order discount = 3 % of subtotal when subtotal >= 500.00.
- Allocation: in integer pennies, share_i = floor(D x net_i / subtotal); leftover pennies go one each to lines with the largest remainder (exact fraction comparison, earlier line wins ties).
- Tax per line on (net - share) at 20 / 5 / 0 %, rounded, summed. total = subtotal - D + tax.
- Discounts are reported as negative values; zero is `0.00`, never `-0.00`. All amounts formatted with exactly two decimals.

**Orders: shipped, fulfil, invoice, report**
- Shipped so far for an order line = sum of `-quantity` over negative movements with that SKU whose note is exactly `order <ID>` (upper case ID), capped at the ordered quantity, over all dates.
- Status: `complete` when nothing is owed on any line, `open` when nothing has shipped on any line, else `partial`.
- `fulfil ORDER DATE`: per line, available = min(balance after all movements dated <= DATE, every balance after a movement dated > DATE), floored at 0; ship = min(owed, available). Appends `DATE SKU -N order <ID>` for each line with N > 0 (in order-line order), then prints the result lines and the status computed after shipping. Nothing to ship is not an error (exit 0, file untouched). DATE before the order's date is refused (exit 1); an unknown order is refused (exit 1).
- `invoice`: `price_order` on the order restricted to shipped quantities (lines with 0 shipped omitted); its own subtotal decides the order discount. Nothing shipped -> refused (exit 1).
- `report`: rows sorted by (date, integer value of the order number, order id string). Text: `ID DATE CUSTOMER STATUS SHIPPED/ORDERED QUOTED INVOICED`. CSV (via `csv` module, `\n` line ends): header `order,date,customer,status,ordered,shipped,quoted,invoiced`. JSON: array of objects with those keys, `ordered`/`shipped` numbers, amounts strings. No orders -> text prints nothing, csv prints only the header, json prints `[]`.

**CLI**
- Commands: `stock`, `low`, `history SKU`, `receive DATE SKU QTY [NOTE]`, `ship DATE SKU QTY [NOTE]`, `quote ORDER`, `fulfil ORDER DATE`, `invoice ORDER`, `report`.
- `--dir DIR` and `--dir=DIR` are accepted anywhere for every command (also in the middle of receive/ship/fulfil arguments); repeated options: last one wins. `--json` only on stock/low/history/quote/invoice; `--format text|csv|json` (or `--format=...`) only on report. For stock/low/history/quote/invoice/report, any other argument starting with `-` is an unknown option (exit 2). For receive/ship/fulfil every argument other than `--dir` and its value is positional, taken as typed. No option abbreviations. A missing option value or bad `--format` value is exit 2.
- Exit 2 (usage message on stderr): no command, unknown command, wrong number of positional args, unknown option, bad option value, a malformed or non-existent DATE argument (receive/ship/fulfil). Then files are read (exit 2 for missing catalogue, missing/unreadable folder, not-a-folder, non-UTF-8). Then the request: exit 1 for file mistakes and refusals (unknown SKU/order, bad quantity such as `-5`, `0`, `5x`, a note containing `\n` or `\r`, negative stock at any point in date order, fulfil date before the order date, invoice with nothing shipped). Every error: message on stderr prefixed `stockroom: `, nothing on stdout.
- SKU and ORDER arguments are case-insensitive (normalised to upper case); an ORDER argument that is not a valid order id is simply "not in orders.txt" (exit 1).
- receive/ship: the note argument is trimmed (space/tab); an empty note means no note. The line written and printed is `DATE SKU +N[ NOTE]` / `DATE SKU -N[ NOTE]`, SKU upper case. The full new movement list (existing + new one at the end) is re-validated before writing; on refusal the file is byte-for-byte unchanged. Appending is done in binary: if the file exists, is non-empty and does not end with `\n`, write `\n` first; then the line plus `\n`. A missing `movements.txt` is created.
- JSON output: `json.dumps(..., indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)` followed by a newline. Stdout is written as UTF-8 regardless of locale.
- Broken pipe: catch `BrokenPipeError` (and flush failures), redirect stdout to devnull, exit 0, no traceback.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests use the standard library `unittest` only (runnable with `python -m unittest discover -s tests`; pytest may also run them but must not be required).
- Library tests per parser (every rule above, positive and negative, checking `.line` and that the message contains `line N`), stock levels/status/buy, and pricing (the worked example SO-1001 -> subtotal 148.47, tax 28.80, total 177.27; an order >= £500 exercising the penny allocation and tie-breaking; half-up rounding at `0.005`).
- CLI tests run `stockroom.cli.main(argv)` in-process against temp folders, capturing stdout/stderr and the exit code, plus at least one subprocess test via `python -m stockroom` (exit codes, broken pipe with `| head -1`).
- One end-to-end check that `pip install .` into a fresh venv yields both `import stockroom` and a working `stockroom` command.
- Tests for the `## Original request` examples verbatim (the `stock` and `quote SO-1001` outputs shown there).

## Out of Scope

- Third-party dependencies of any kind (runtime or required for tests).
- Editing or deleting existing lines in any file; only appending movements.
- Locking against concurrent writers, currencies other than pounds, tax-inclusive prices, partial-line pricing rules beyond those described.
- A `--help` system beyond a short usage message on errors.

- [ ] BOM is ignored; CRLF and LF both work; blank and `#` comment lines are skipped; a lone `\r` and `str.splitlines` separators are not line breaks.
- [ ] Price, reorder, quantities, SKU, order id and date validation follows the regexes and ranges in Implementation Decisions (e.g. `12.505`, `1,000.00`, `-3`, `abc`, `2024-02-30`, `+0`, `1_000` are rejected).
- [ ] Duplicate SKU in catalogue, duplicate order id, SKU repeated within an order, and unknown SKUs in movements/orders are mistakes on the right line.
- [ ] Stock going below zero in date order (same-day movements in file order) is reported on the offending movement's line.
- [ ] `stock_levels` covers every catalogue SKU (0 when unmoved).
- [ ] `stockroom stock` and `stockroom stock --json` match the spec (the example output reproduces exactly).
- [ ] `stockroom low [--json]` lists low/out products with BUY = `max(1, 2*reorder - onhand)`.
- [ ] `stockroom history SKU [--json]` prints `DATE DELTA BALANCE[ NOTE]` in counting order; unknown SKU exits 1.

- [ ] `stockroom quote ORDER [--json]` reproduces the spec example exactly; unknown order exits 1.

- Read bytes, decode strict UTF-8 (failure -> exit 2), drop one leading U+FEFF. Split on `\n` only, then remove one trailing `\r` per line (so CRLF works; a lone `\r` elsewhere is ordinary content). Do NOT use `str.splitlines()`.
- "Whitespace" for trimming, blank-line detection, comment detection and separators means space and tab only. A line is blank if it is empty after trimming; it is a comment if it starts with `#` after leading space/tab.
- Numbers are ASCII digits only (regexes, never bare `int()`, which accepts `1_000` and non-ASCII digits).
  - price: `^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]{1,2})?$` and >= 0.01 (`12.` and `.5` are mistakes; leading zeros allowed).
  - reorder: `^[0-9]+$` (no sign).
  - movement quantity: `^[+-]?[0-9]+$`, non-zero (`0`, `+0`, `-00` are mistakes).
  - order line quantity: `^[0-9]+$`, >= 1.
- SKU: `^[A-Za-z]{2,4}-[0-9]{3}$`, stored upper case. Order id: `^[Ss][Oo]-[0-9]+$`, stored upper case (digits kept as typed). Date: `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$` and a real calendar date.
- Catalogue: 4 or 5 `|`-separated fields; tax case-insensitive, stored lower case; duplicate SKU is reported on the second line.
- Movements: at least 3 whitespace-separated fields; note = rest of the line after the quantity field, trimmed. Lines are first all parsed in file order (first syntax error wins); then the stock check runs over the movements stable-sorted by date and reports the first movement (in that order) that takes a product below zero, by its own file line number.
- Orders: exactly 4 fields; LINES split on `,` (empty piece is a mistake); duplicate SKU within an order and duplicate order id are mistakes.
- `ParseError(ValueError)` has `.line`; `str(err)` starts with `line N: ` followed by a short description. The CLI prints `stockroom: <file>: line N: ...` on stderr.
- Commands read only their files, in the order catalogue, movements, orders; the first file mistake wins.

**Stock**
- Movements count stably sorted by date. `stock_levels` covers every catalogue SKU. Status: `out` = 0, `low` = 0 < onhand <= reorder, `ok` otherwise. `low` BUY = `max(1, 2*reorder - onhand)`. Sorting "by SKU" = plain string order of the upper-case SKU.

**Pricing** (`Decimal`, `ROUND_HALF_UP` to `0.01` at every rounding step)
- Per line: gross = qty x unit; volume discount 10 % if qty >= 50, else 5 % if qty >= 10, else 0; net = gross - discount.
- subtotal = sum of nets; order discount = 3 % of subtotal when subtotal >= 500.00.
- Allocation: in integer pennies, share_i = floor(D x net_i / subtotal); leftover pennies go one each to lines with the largest remainder (exact fraction comparison, earlier line wins ties).
- Tax per line on (net - share) at 20 / 5 / 0 %, rounded, summed. total = subtotal - D + tax.
- Discounts are reported as negative values; zero is `0.00`, never `-0.00`. All amounts formatted with exactly two decimals.

**Orders: shipped, fulfil, invoice, report**
- Shipped so far for an order line = sum of `-quantity` over negative movements with that SKU whose note is exactly `order <ID>` (upper case ID), capped at the ordered quantity, over all dates.
- Status: `complete` when nothing is owed on any line, `open` when nothing has shipped on any line, else `partial`.
- `fulfil ORDER DATE`: per line, available = min(balance after all movements dated <= DATE, every balance after a movement dated > DATE), floored at 0; ship = min(owed, available). Appends `DATE SKU -N order <ID>` for each line with N > 0 (in order-line order), then prints the result lines and the status computed after shipping. Nothing to ship is not an error (exit 0, file untouched). DATE before the order's date is refused (exit 1); an unknown order is refused (exit 1).
- `invoice`: `price_order` on the order restricted to shipped quantities (lines with 0 shipped omitted); its own subtotal decides the order discount. Nothing shipped -> refused (exit 1).
- `report`: rows sorted by (date, integer value of the order number, order id string). Text: `ID DATE CUSTOMER STATUS SHIPPED/ORDERED QUOTED INVOICED`. CSV (via `csv` module, `\n` line ends): header `order,date,customer,status,ordered,shipped,quoted,invoiced`. JSON: array of objects with those keys, `ordered`/`shipped` numbers, amounts strings. No orders -> text prints nothing, csv prints only the header, json prints `[]`.

**CLI**
- Commands: `stock`, `low`, `history SKU`, `receive DATE SKU QTY [NOTE]`, `ship DATE SKU QTY [NOTE]`, `quote ORDER`, `fulfil ORDER DATE`, `invoice ORDER`, `report`.
- `--dir DIR` and `--dir=DIR` are accepted anywhere for every command (also in the middle of receive/ship/fulfil arguments); repeated options: last one wins. `--json` only on stock/low/history/quote/invoice; `--format text|csv|json` (or `--format=...`) only on report. For stock/low/history/quote/invoice/report, any other argument starting with `-` is an unknown option (exit 2). For receive/ship/fulfil every argument other than `--dir` and its value is positional, taken as typed. No option abbreviations. A missing option value or bad `--format` value is exit 2.
- Exit 2 (usage message on stderr): no command, unknown command, wrong number of positional args, unknown option, bad option value, a malformed or non-existent DATE argument (receive/ship/fulfil). Then files are read (exit 2 for missing catalogue, missing/unreadable folder, not-a-folder, non-UTF-8). Then the request: exit 1 for file mistakes and refusals (unknown SKU/order, bad quantity such as `-5`, `0`, `5x`, a note containing `\n` or `\r`, negative stock at any point in date order, fulfil date before the order date, invoice with nothing shipped). Every error: message on stderr prefixed `stockroom: `, nothing on stdout.
- SKU and ORDER arguments are case-insensitive (normalised to upper case); an ORDER argument that is not a valid order id is simply "not in orders.txt" (exit 1).
- receive/ship: the note argument is trimmed (space/tab); an empty note means no note. The line written and printed is `DATE SKU +N[ NOTE]` / `DATE SKU -N[ NOTE]`, SKU upper case. The full new movement list (existing + new one at the end) is re-validated before writing; on refusal the file is byte-for-byte unchanged. Appending is done in binary: if the file exists, is non-empty and does not end with `\n`, write `\n` first; then the line plus `\n`. A missing `movements.txt` is created.
- JSON output: `json.dumps(..., indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)` followed by a newline. Stdout is written as UTF-8 regardless of locale.
- Broken pipe: catch `BrokenPipeError` (and flush failures), redirect stdout to devnull, exit 0, no traceback.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests use the standard library `unittest` only (runnable with `python -m unittest discover -s tests`; pytest may also run them but must not be required).
- Library tests per parser (every rule above, positive and negative, checking `.line` and that the message contains `line N`), stock levels/status/buy, and pricing (the worked example SO-1001 -> subtotal 148.47, tax 28.80, total 177.27; an order >= £500 exercising the penny allocation and tie-breaking; half-up rounding at `0.005`).
- CLI tests run `stockroom.cli.main(argv)` in-process against temp folders, capturing stdout/stderr and the exit code, plus at least one subprocess test via `python -m stockroom` (exit codes, broken pipe with `| head -1`).
- One end-to-end check that `pip install .` into a fresh venv yields both `import stockroom` and a working `stockroom` command.
- Tests for the `## Original request` examples verbatim (the `stock` and `quote SO-1001` outputs shown there).

## Out of Scope

- Third-party dependencies of any kind (runtime or required for tests).
- Editing or deleting existing lines in any file; only appending movements.
- Locking against concurrent writers, currencies other than pounds, tax-inclusive prices, partial-line pricing rules beyond those described.
- A `--help` system beyond a short usage message on errors.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pip install .` in a fresh venv on Python >= 3.9 installs the importable `stockroom` package and the `stockroom` command; no third-party runtime dependencies.
- [ ] `parse_catalog`, `parse_movements`, `parse_orders` return the documented types/attributes (Decimal price, int reorder, `datetime.date`, upper-case SKU/order id, note `""` when absent, lines as `(sku, qty)` tuples in order).
- [ ] Every malformed line in each file raises `stockroom.ParseError` (a `ValueError`) whose `.line` is the 1-based physical line number (blank/comment lines counted) and whose message contains `line N`.
- [ ] BOM is ignored; CRLF and LF both work; blank and `#` comment lines are skipped; a lone `\r` and `str.splitlines` separators are not line breaks.
- [ ] Price, reorder, quantities, SKU, order id and date validation follows the regexes and ranges in Implementation Decisions (e.g. `12.505`, `1,000.00`, `-3`, `abc`, `2024-02-30`, `+0`, `1_000` are rejected).
- [ ] Duplicate SKU in catalogue, duplicate order id, SKU repeated within an order, and unknown SKUs in movements/orders are mistakes on the right line.
- [ ] Stock going below zero in date order (same-day movements in file order) is reported on the offending movement's line.
- [ ] `stock_levels` covers every catalogue SKU (0 when unmoved).
- [ ] `stockroom stock` and `stockroom stock --json` match the spec (the example output reproduces exactly).
- [ ] `stockroom low [--json]` lists low/out products with BUY = `max(1, 2*reorder - onhand)`.
- [ ] `stockroom history SKU [--json]` prints `DATE DELTA BALANCE[ NOTE]` in counting order; unknown SKU exits 1.
- [ ] `receive`/`ship` append the correct line (adding a missing trailing newline first, creating the file if absent), print it, and refuse (exit 1, file byte-identical) unknown SKUs, bad quantities (incl. dash-led), notes with line breaks, and any negative stock at any point in date order.
- [ ] `price_order` follows the six pricing rules exactly (half-up rounding, 5 %/10 % volume discount, 3 % order discount at >= £500, floor-plus-largest-remainder allocation with earlier-line tie-break, per-line tax); all amounts are 2-dp Decimals and discounts <= 0.
- [ ] `stockroom quote ORDER [--json]` reproduces the spec example exactly; unknown order exits 1.
- [ ] `stockroom fulfil ORDER DATE` ships min(owed, available-on-DATE, minimum later balance), appends one `DATE SKU -N order ID` per shipped line, prints `SKU shipped N backordered M` lines and `status open|partial|complete`; date before order date or unknown order exits 1.
- [ ] `stockroom invoice ORDER [--json]` prices shipped quantities with the `invoice ` header prefix and omits unshipped lines; nothing shipped exits 1.
- [ ] `stockroom report` in text, csv and json formats with the specified columns, keys, types and sort order.
- [ ] `--dir` works anywhere on the line for every command; receive/ship/fulfil take every other argument as typed.
- [ ] Exit codes: 0 success; 1 file mistakes and refusals (stderr names file and line, stdout empty); 2 for command-line errors (checked first, before reading files) and unreadable files (missing catalogue, missing folder, non-UTF-8).
- [ ] Each command reads only the files it needs (a broken `orders.txt` does not affect `stock`; a broken `movements.txt` does not affect `quote`).
- [ ] `stockroom stock | head -1` exits 0 with no traceback.
- [ ] A stdlib `unittest` suite covers all of the above and passes on Python 3.9+.
